upload.title: The Machine Behind Walmart: How Logistics Beat Kmart, and Now Amazon
upload.description:
Walmart didn't win with better stores. It won with everything that happened before a product reached the shelf: its own distribution centers, its own trucks, cross-docking, a private satellite network and Retail Link. Now it is rebuilding that machine with robots, automated fulfillment centers, stores that double as warehouses, and drones.

This documentary follows the system from a 1962 store in Rogers, Arkansas to Walmart's 2026 automation results, using academic research, company filings and official footage.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:53 The Road Nobody Wanted
2:21 Goods That Never Stop
3:19 Information Moves Faster Than Trucks
4:36 The Wrong Machine
5:17 Inside the New Machine
6:46 The Weapon Hiding in Plain Sight
8:00 The Payoff

Research and sources:
- Holmes, T. J. (2011). The Diffusion of Wal-Mart and Economies of Density. Econometrica, 79(1), 253-302. Store and DC data: users.econ.umn.edu/~holmes/data/WalMart/
- Stalk, G., Evans, P., & Shulman, L. E. (1992). Competing on Capabilities: The New Rules of Corporate Strategy. Harvard Business Review, 70(2), 57-69.
- Harvard Business School case: Lou Pritchett, Negotiating the P&G Relationship with Wal-Mart.
- Walmart corporate history; CIO, 45 Years of Wal-Mart History: A Technology Time Line.
- Walmart 2023 Investment Community Meeting (April 4, 2023).
- Symbotic Form 8-K (January 2025): acquisition of Walmart's Advanced Systems and Robotics business.
- Walmart and Wing drone delivery expansion (January 2026).
- Walmart Q2 FY27 earnings release and call (August 2026).

Footage: Walmart, Symbotic, KNAPP, Wing, Alert Innovation, BusinessWire (Walmart press), Amazon, archival Kmart footage. Map: Census ZCTA centroids, Holmes store data.
Narration, music and sound design: ElevenLabs.
